newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN QUIET THURSDAY TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN QUIET THURSDAY TRADE.

text.p: Short term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market continued mixed in quiet trading on Thursday morning, dealers said.

"We were expecting the market to be short because there haven't been any maturities in the last couple of days but surprisingly it's a bit liquid, I'm not quite sure where the money is coming from," commented one dealer.
Discount houses were on Thursday buying treasury bills from the central bank at 19.60 percent and selling them in the market at a steady 19.50 percent.
NCD bills redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought firmer at 23.5 percent from 20.75 percent and sold at 20.50 percent, marginally up from 20.25.
Bankers acceptances were buying at a steady 20.50 percent, but their selling rate eased to 19.50 from 20 percent.
Call money, which fluctuated between 19 and 19.50 percent the previous day, was on Thursday quoted at around 20 percent in a market which opened in surplus of Z$26 million.
